clue.text: This drop is sweet, but it can be hallucinogenic

definitions.text: This drop is sweet, but it can be hallucinogenic

parts.words: This drop is sweet, but it can be hallucinogenic
parts.note: the first half points to a boiled sweet called an ___ drop, the second to the slang name for LSD

explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a sharp-flavoured British boiled sweet; on its own the word is slang for the hallucinogen LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the drug LSD, and the first word of a sharp boiled sweet's name.

clue.text: Intercourse, or the opposite

definitions.meaning: as a verb or noun, conversation or talking together
a logical reversal of a statement, its contrary

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to talk with someone; as a noun it means a statement's reverse.

clue.text: River sport

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England flowing through Durham and Sunderland
to sport a hat is to have it on, display it

explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England. 'Sport' is a verb here: to sport clothes is to have them on.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a Durham river, and a verb for having clothes on, as in sporting a jacket.

clue.text: With a drink problem one may lose direction and become offensive

indicators.note: the clue says the answer, once it loses a compass point, turns into the word for offensive; so that point goes back inside

parts.note: violent, as in an offensive or aggressive act
N, north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A drunkard who loses his way and turns aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written backwards: 'one may lose direction' says the answer, minus N, becomes VIOLENT. Building it, N goes into VIOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word meaning given to wine or drunkenness, from Latin vinum, wine.

clue.text: Stretch various drapes

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the word drapes in assorted arrangements

explanation.surface: Curtains of different kinds are pulled out across a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to spread something out is to stretch it over an area.

clue.text: Railwayman led vibrant development

indicators.note: development as change or growth, so the letters of led vibrant are reworked

explanation.surface: A railway worker headed some lively project.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornelius Vanderbilt was a nineteenth-century American railroad magnate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornelius Vanderbilt built a fortune from US railroads, so he is a famous railway tycoon.

clue.text: Does he offer tea on one's last trip?

definitions.text: Does he offer tea on one's last trip?

parts.note: char is informal British slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone serves a cuppa on the final journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Charon ferried the dead across the Styx, the last trip; CHAR is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythological ferryman who carries the souls of the dead across to the underworld.

clue.text: False god not heard to be working

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for a false god is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: an idol is an image worshipped as a false god

explanation.surface: A false deity is silent and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone idle is not working, sitting unemployed.

clue.text: The same as 151

parts.note: CL is the Roman numeral for 150, and the remaining unit is one
the unit left after 150 is one

explanation.surface: Something is identical to a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 151 is not a clue reference here: it is read as 150 in Roman numerals followed by the word for a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy identical to its original is exactly the same as it.

clue.text: Disparaged halfback eating fruit

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside
back means the word for half is turned round

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A rugby or football halfback is criticised while snacking on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfback' looks like a sports position, but it splits into 'half' and 'back'; 'back' turns the French-derived prefix round, and 'eating' wraps it round the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeached is used loosely, in an older sense, to mean called into question or discredited.

clue.text: Rose loved fried fish

indicators.note: fried suggests the letters of Rose loved are cooked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose enjoyed some fried fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dover sole is a prized flatfish caught in the English Channel.

clue.text: Song expressing gravity in calamitous situation

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: dire means calamitous or dreadful
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A song that conveys solemnity during a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead.

clue.text: Prosper in cheerful time of year, as they say

indicators.note: as they say means the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: merry May, a cheerful month of the year

explanation.surface: Thriving in a happy season, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prosper' looks like a verb but is the first name of the French writer Prosper Mérimée, author of Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosper is the first name of Mérimée, the French author whose novella became the opera Carmen.

clue.text: Criminal underground starts many a feud in America

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Gangland violence begins with many disputes in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is a secret criminal organisation, an underworld network.

clue.text: See 27
Arrested 30 for imprisonment that could be vile

annotationWithheld.why: Arrested 30 for imprisonment that could be vile: DURANCE is RAN inside DUCE (30, Mussolini), but 'Arrested' must give RAN IN (run in) and signal the insertion at once, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Arrested 30 for imprisonment that could be vile

clue.text: Former French island's outcast

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: Someone banished from a former French island.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished from their home country, an outcast.

clue.text: Ally has no right to be an evil one

indicators.note: has no means a letter is dropped from the word for ally

parts.note: a friend is an ally

explanation.surface: A companion who lacks righteousness turns wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is a devil or wicked person, an evil being.

clue.text: Company that backs anything

indicators.note: backs means the word for anything is read in the other direction

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A firm that supports any venture at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' is from the saying 'two's company'. OWT is Yorkshire dialect for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd': a pair makes company.

clue.text: Hope lion could be 4

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of Hope lion might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Bob Hope or a lion might turn out to be a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to 4 down, whose definition is 'With a drink problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover of wine, which fits loosely with a drinker described in 4 down.

clue.text: Nice one for revolting tribe

indicators.note: revolting suggests the letters rising up and changing places

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pleasant person swapped for a rebellious people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni, led by Boudicca, revolted against Roman rule in Britain, so 'revolting' does double duty in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe in what is now Norfolk.

clue.text: Cancellations certain to appear in The Times

indicators.note: to appear in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: eras are times or periods
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Something is sure to be crossed out in a famous London newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper but is just ERAS, periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasures are rubbings-out or deletions, things cancelled.

clue.text: Boy twice seen by a medic in the States

indicators.note: twice means the boy's name is written two times over

parts.note: Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: A lad seen two times by an American doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medic' is not a doctor but medick, a clover-like plant; in America lucerne is called alfalfa.
explanation.definitionFit: Medic, or medick, is a fodder plant genus; lucerne goes by this name in North America.

clue.text: Commotion as fire spread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters of as fire scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out as a blaze spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraise is an old dialect word for a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Soldier in love with a girl is slow

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An infatuated soldier with a girlfriend takes things slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning slowly.

clue.text: Compound reportedly given for working unsociable hours

indicators.note: reportedly means a spoken phrase gives a word of the same sound

parts.note: a night rate is the higher pay given for working through the night

explanation.surface: A chemical substance said to be paid to night-shift workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical compound, a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Boat with King Charles at the stern

parts.note: CR, Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher for King Charles
aft means at the back or stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying a king at its rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is any boat or vessel.

clue.text: Order into detention having teeth

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CB, confined to barracks, a military punishment of detention
OM, the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An instruction to lock up someone with teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: CB stands for 'confined to barracks', a military punishment; OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A grooming tool with a row of teeth, here described by what it has.

clue.text: Broadcasting intended for weight watchers?

parts.note: a radio transmission method whose name, read literally, suggests changing one's size, which dieters would want

explanation.walkthrough: A radio method that varies the strength of the signal; dieters also aim to vary their bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: The AM radio technique that varies the strength of a carrier wave to transmit sound.

clue.text: Dean captures heart of chorister

indicators.note: heart of means the outer letters of the word for chorister are dropped

parts.note: a chorister is a singer in a choir

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean wins over a choirboy's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: W. R. Inge, the 'Gloomy Dean', was Dean of St Paul's Cathedral in London. 'captures' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: William Inge was a famous Dean of St Paul's in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: She's climbing mountains — but not all the way

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading the letters upwards
not all the way means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Andes are a mountain range

explanation.surface: A woman scaling a mountain range but stopping short of the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name, so a female pronoun stands for it.

clue.text: Leader with strength of voice in Italy

definitions.text: Leader with strength of voice in Italy

parts.words: Leader with strength of voice in Italy
parts.note: an Italian ruler known as Il Duce, famed for bombastic speeches from the balcony

explanation.walkthrough: Benito Mussolini, Italy's Fascist dictator, was famous for his loud, bombastic oratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's Fascist dictator, called Il Duce, meaning the leader.

clue.text: Force to bend over to gather up the fragments

parts.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force
to lean is to bend or tilt over

explanation.surface: A force makes something bow down to collect the scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather leftover bits, originally grain after the harvest.
